subsection.name: Writing the Controller
subsection.p: The controller is the object which binds the model and the view together.

subsection.name: Controller responsabilities
Controls
subsection.p:
Controls are used by the Scope framework to transmit String constants representing commands from Views, SubControllers and Controllers to a Controller.
Setting up a Control:
Declare the control's String constant either in the control that will handle it or in the view that will issue the Control.
/** * A Control ID. */ public static final String VALIDATE_LOGIN_CONTROL_ID = "Login";
NOTE: Each Controller that extends BasicController will have a built in Control String constant called EXIT_CONTROL_ID . Views can issue this Control to exit the application when the view is closed.
Triggering the Control:
issueControl(Control c) can be called from a View.
For Swing, a common way to trigger an issue control is to attach the Control to an SComponent.
Handling the Control:
handleControl(Control c) can be called from a sub-controller or locally within a controller.
If a subcontroller calls handleControl(Control c) on a Control that is not handled locally in the subcontroller's doHandleControl() method the Control is automatically forwarded to the parent controller.

subsection.name: Hierarchy of controllers
View-specific Controllers
subsection.p: Depending on the type of view used in your application, you will have to use different types of controllers.

The following base classes are provided in Scope:
View type Base class for the controller
Swing
org.scopemvc.controller.basic.BasicController
Servlet/JSP/XML+XSLT org.scopemvc.controller.servlet.ServletController
